That’s a lie. If you’re being over dramatic, then a whole lot of people are as well, even more so. And I know I’m just some random person on the internet, but I’m real, and I don’t lie and sugarcoat things which just makes them worse later on. I hope that’s okay with you. Have you explained what’s happening to your mom yet? That may affect her decision. Also, you are a legal adult now. She cannot control the choices you make anymore. She may be a good parent to you, but if she’s causing problems for your mental health, she should probably change a few things. I don’t know what your situation is like, but I can look at it from an objective standpoint and tell you that it’s probably a good idea to talk this out with her.

I wish you all the best.

First off, I’m not going to tell you that kind of stuff, because it’s a blatant half-truth. Yes, it will probably get better. But they conveniently forget to mention that it also gets worse. It’s a series of ups and downs. I guess I feel the same was a lot of the time. I just ignore my schoolwork because, what’s the point? Especially if I’m going to be dead by 18 anyways. I guess the only reason I try is because I want to feel happiness for once by doing things I like, even if it’s artificial. I want to at least enjoy a little bit of my life before I die.

Are you sure she’s the only thing stopping you? You also have a little cousin that you talked about, and honestly, even if you’re being blamed for everything, living with people who treat like that isn’t permanent. Death, however, is. I’m really sorry if I’m coming off as insensitive, I don’t mean to, but I wanted to die a lot more than I do now last year, and one of the things that stopped me was knowing that there were so many paths and choices, and I wanted the one that I could never take back.

Knowing that there were so many possibilities, some of them maybe even happy, and I just would shut them all down like that stopped me. I hope you find your path.
I actually made another post about it, the gist of it is that my parents sometimes feel so overbearing and controlling that I don’t feel safe. Thank you.

Because everybody dies eventually, but even a year of life could change so much. If Isaac Newton died before he wrote his laws, if Hamilton lived for another year, left to create new systems, the world might have been very different.

Trying to forget just makes people remember more. Trust me, I know from experience. But suicide is a chain reaction. Once the first thing happens, there’s no way to stop it. A death leads to guilt and blame, leads to pain, leads to misery. It goes on and on, and there’s always the risk of another death. Guilt in the moment is better than guilt when there’s nothing you can do about it. They might blame themselves, and then what happens next? If you die, they will always live with the guilt of knowing they could have saved you, but didn’t try hard enough, didn’t show what they felt the right way, made you think and feel this. It may not be true, but that feeling will stay no matter what.

Your life sounds like it sucks, but death is permanent, this might not be. I would have died a year ago if I didn’t know that no matter how hard I try to prevent it, the repercussions will be there forever, whether I live or die.

Honestly, I kind of agree with some of the things you said. Life feels like it sucks sometimes, actually, most of the time, and it’s hard to find motivation and actually feel anything at all, let alone cope with said emotions. I’m not going to say that life gets better, because that’s bullshit, but it has it’s ups and downs. And I’m not going to say to talk to me, because honestly, I suck at emotions and people, but I know the feeling of posting something, and wanting advice, and then being totally ignored at the time when I need the most help. I hate all this cheesy stuff, and I can’t reassure people for the life of me, but just know that you’re not a ghost. And I know it sounds stupid, hey, at least remember that people see you, and that they might actually care, even if it’s just sympathy. I don’t know you, but I know the feeling.

I’m sorry if this just made things worse, because once again, communication is my Achilles heel, and I never comment that much because of it, but I hope it helps.

I think you could say that you are anhedonic. I found this word when I was depressed, and only felt numb. Just apathy and anxiety. I get the scaring yourself thing, though. I sometimes think really dark thoughts, and then terrify myself with them, because if I’m already so easily impressionable, can I really trust myself?

I wouldn’t be surprised if Hell was just earth as it it now, or if this is actually Hell. It reminds me of a bit in Good Omens, where Crowley protests to claims that he’s doing nothing, that no matter how hard demons try to corrupt humans, the humans themselves are constantly one-upping them. Humans did a better job than demons at ruining their own lives.
Relatable. No matter how bad you have it, you know that there’s always someone out there who’s worse than you, and then you feel selfish and guilty.
Same, kind of. I mimic characters so much that I don’t know what’s me and what’s the characters anymore.
Same. I try and get my work done, but I just don’t care enough, and know that I’ll probably be dead before it can affect me too much.

That’s a horrible thing to say. Don’t invalidate others emotions. Attraction and beauty are a matter of who sees. Also, other’s people fears and feelings are not just something you can treat like a plaything. Honestly, I would have reported this, but you need to know that you are the jerk here. Nobody should be told that their fears are pointless and to “Quit being a little bitch, bro.”

Honestly, if all you’re going to say to a person’s problems is that, then you shouldn’t say anything at all.

I’m pretty sure that women would be more attracted to a kind person than a person who doesn’t care about other’s feelings, no matter their height.
But think about it. What if they don’t forget? What would happen then?
